name: Integralism
summary: Catholic integralism holds that political authority should be ordered to humanity's spiritual end, so the state must publicly profess and protect the Catholic faith and be guided by the Church in spiritual matters. It rejects separation of church and state, popular sovereignty, religious neutrality and unrestricted freedom of speech and worship, while accepting several forms of government. On economics it follows Catholic social teaching: private property and family rights, cooperation between classes, workers' associations and a limited duty of the state toward the poor.
scope: Catholic integralism, as set out in the papal teaching of Pius IX and Leo XIII (Quanta Cura, Immortale Dei, Rerum Novarum) and as revived by contemporary writers such as Waldstein, Pink, Vermeule, Crean and Fimister. Excludes Brazilian Integralism (a separate fascist-leaning movement), Spanish Integrism's regional politics, Maurras's integral nationalism and Ken Wilber's integral theory.

furtherReading.title: Immortale Dei (Leo XIII, 1885)
furtherReading.note: Foundational encyclical on the Christian constitution of states.

furtherReading.title: Rerum Novarum (Leo XIII, 1891)
furtherReading.note: The Catholic social teaching on property, labour and class.

furtherReading.title: Quanta Cura (Pius IX, 1864)
furtherReading.note: The encyclical condemning liberty of conscience and religious neutrality.

keyFigures.name: Leo XIII
keyFigures.role: Pope whose encyclicals (Immortale Dei, Rerum Novarum) are core texts of integralist political teaching.

keyFigures.name: Pius IX
keyFigures.role: Pope who issued Quanta Cura and the Syllabus of Errors against liberalism.

keyFigures.name: Adrian Vermeule
keyFigures.role: Legal scholar who popularised common good constitutionalism and is linked to contemporary integralism.

raise-minimum-wage.rationale: Rerum Novarum says wages must suffice to support a frugal worker and his family and that the state may step in where agreement fails, which supports a living-wage floor.

markets-allocate-better.rationale: Contemporary integralists criticise liberalism and capitalism, and Rerum Novarum subordinates economic life to justice and the common good, though it defends private property and free wage agreements.

public-ownership.rationale: Rerum Novarum treats private ownership as a natural right and rejects collective ownership, so nationalising whole industries is not a default, though state action for the common good is allowed.

tax-the-wealthy.rationale: Rerum Novarum stresses fair taxation yet forbids burdens that effectively confiscate property, so significantly higher taxes on the wealthy are disfavoured.

unions-good.rationale: Rerum Novarum strongly encourages workers' associations, including mixed worker-employer bodies, as long as religion and morality come first.

property-fundamental.rationale: Rerum Novarum calls the inviolability of private property the first principle of improving workers' condition, but integralism makes property serve the common good, so it is not absolute.

worker-ownership.rationale: Rerum Novarum wants property spread among workers but rejects collective ownership; mandatory collective ownership of firms is not an integralist position, nor is it condemned.

strong-leader.rationale: Integralism favours authority ordered to the common good, with no form of government condemned, but it also stresses lawful rule and fatherly governance, so a gridlock-bypassing strongman is not a tenet.

state-harmful.rationale: Immortale Dei treats civil government as divinely grounded and necessary for the community's welfare; the state is neither unnecessary nor harmful.

legalize-sex-work.rationale: Law is meant to promote virtue and sound morals, and Catholic teaching condemns prostitution, so integralists would keep it illegal.

decide-locally.rationale: Rerum Novarum treats the family and associations as societies with their own rights not to be absorbed by the state, a subsidiarity logic favouring lower levels.

rehabilitation.rationale: Quanta Cura defends the state's power to punish violators, while Catholic teaching also values reform, so the two aims are balanced.

traditional-family.rationale: Immortale Dei treats marriage as holy and indissoluble and Rerum Novarum calls the family a society older than the state with its own rights.

same-sex-marriage.rationale: Marriage is described as holy, lifelong and indissoluble, and the state may not redefine it; Catholic doctrine underpins public law for integralists.

more-religion-public.rationale: Immortale Dei says the state must publicly profess and protect the true religion and that ignoring God is a public crime.

preserve-national-culture.rationale: Integralists value Christian tradition in public life, but their loyalty is to the Church and a universal faith more than to national culture as such.

gradual-change.rationale: The integralist strategy involves both patient work within liberal institutions and a long-term aim of restoring a Catholic state; established institutions are respected only if they are ordered to the right end.

empower-international-orgs.rationale: Integralists criticise liberalism's secular international order; their universal authority is the Church, not the UN, though they do not reject international cooperation as such.

nation-first.rationale: Integralism stresses the common good under the spiritual end and the universal Church, while accepting nations; the sources do not settle the question.

revolution-justified.rationale: Immortale Dei condemns rebellion against legitimate rulers, though the order is rooted in authority from God rather than the people.

experts-over-public.rationale: Integralism holds authority should be ordered to truth and the common good rather than majority wish, which favours rule by the competent; no explicit statement on experts.

central-planning.rationale: Rerum Novarum limits state intervention to what is needed and defends property and free wage agreement; full central planning is not an integralist position.

tax-inheritance.rationale: Rerum Novarum grounds property in the family's need and bars confiscatory taxes, which counts against heavy inheritance taxation.

widespread-small-property.rationale: Rerum Novarum presents widespread property among workers as a way to narrow the gap between rich and poor and as a family need.

abolish-money-wages.rationale: Rerum Novarum rejects abolition of private property and community of goods and discusses wages as just agreement, so abolishing money and wage labour is rejected.

corporatist-bargaining.rationale: Rerum Novarum encourages mixed workers-and-employers associations, a root of Catholic corporatism, though it wants the state to respect their autonomy rather than set wages and prices.

one-party-rule.rationale: No form of government is condemned, but the ruling principle is the Church's teaching, not a party ideology; integralists do not generally propose a single-party state.

monarchy-legitimate.rationale: Immortale Dei says no form of government is condemned in itself, and monarchy is accepted by the tradition (Leo XIII); some integralists openly favour it.

democracy-best.rationale: Popular sovereignty without reference to God is rejected and the people's share in government is a matter of circumstance, so democracy is not held the best form.

direct-votes.rationale: Quanta Cura and Immortale Dei reject the people's will or public opinion as supreme law; direct popular legislation conflicts with that.

workers-councils.rationale: Political power is meant to rest on authority from God and an order with the Church's guidance, not on workers' councils; class rule is rejected.

political-violence-never.rationale: Rebellion against lawful rulers is condemned, but the just-war tradition and state punishment allow force, so an absolute ban is rejected.

war-builds-character.rationale: Not a theme; Catholic teaching treats war as justified only for just causes, not for character formation.

separate-church-state.rationale: Immortale Dei rejects separation and Quanta Cura condemns governing as if religion did not exist; integralists subordinate state to spiritual ends.

laws-from-scripture.rationale: Integralists want law based on Catholic doctrine, but via natural law and Church teaching rather than by scripture alone, so agreement is not at the maximum.

private-courts-defense.rationale: The state exists for the common good with divinely grounded authority; privatising justice and defence contradicts that.

ethnic-nation.rationale: Integralist unity is based on faith, not ethnicity; Catholic universality counts against ethnic homogeneity as a goal.

class-struggle-history.rationale: Rerum Novarum states class conflict is not natural and that classes depend on each other, with religion the main reconciler.

equal-outcomes.rationale: Rerum Novarum says natural inequality is unavoidable and the goal is justice, not uniformity.

self-interest-moral.rationale: Integralist ethics orders action to the common good and an ultimate spiritual end, so self-interest as such is not a moral good.

duties-before-rights.rationale: Immortale Dei stresses duties of rulers and citizens and calls unrestricted liberty licence, placing obligation above individual claims.

industrial-civilization-disaster.rationale: Rerum Novarum accepts industrial society and aims to reform its injustices rather than condemn it.

restore-past-order.rationale: Integralists aim at an eventual restoration of an integrally Catholic state and reject modern liberal progress narratives.

results-over-ideology.rationale: Integralism judges policy by fidelity to Catholic doctrine and the common good, not by pragmatic results alone.

direct-action.rationale: Contemporary integralists favour working within institutions and Immortale Dei condemns rebellion, so extra-parliamentary direct action is disfavoured.

return-to-foraging.rationale: Nothing in the tradition supports it; Rerum Novarum assumes settled property and labour.

abolish-division-of-labor.rationale: Rerum Novarum treats classes as mutually dependent parts of one body, so abolishing division of labour is rejected.

distribute-by-need.rationale: Wages are governed by agreement within a family-supporting minimum and property is retained; distribution by need as an ultimate principle is rejected, though charity is a duty.

profit-exploitation.rationale: Rerum Novarum warns against exploiting workers but treats ownership and profit as legitimate; the claim that profit is exploitation is not accepted.

dictatorship-of-proletariat.rationale: Class rule and class conflict are rejected in Rerum Novarum, and authority comes from God.

collective-farming.rationale: Rerum Novarum treats land held by the worker as natural property and rejects collective ownership.

capitalism-causes-war.rationale: A Marxist thesis; integralists criticise capitalism but attribute disorder to secular liberalism, not to an inevitable economic logic.

taxation-theft.rationale: Rerum Novarum accepts fair taxation as a state function and only warns against confiscatory levels.

harm-principle.rationale: Law is to promote virtue and truth, and Quanta Cura condemns limiting state punishment to what public peace requires.

individual-rights-only.rationale: The family has rights older than the state and the Church is a perfect society; rights are not held by individuals alone.

exit-over-voice.rationale: Authority is ordered to the common good and God, and voting and exit are not the central checks; the liberal exit framing conflicts.

state-as-business.rationale: Rulers govern as fathers for the community's welfare, not as vendors to customers.

positive-liberty.rationale: Immortale Dei defines true liberty as freedom from error and vice, a substantive conception, though 'material means' emphasis is from Rerum Novarum on wages and property.

hereditarian-race.rationale: Not an integralist teaching; Catholic doctrine on human equality counts against it.

organic-representation.rationale: Rerum Novarum treats family and associations as societies with rights, and Catholic corporatism favours representing such bodies.

total-state.rationale: Rerum Novarum says the state must not absorb the family and should respect associations; the Church is an independent perfect society.

national-rebirth.rationale: Integralists speak of restoring the Catholic order after liberal decadence, but a national rebirth in the fascist sense is not their framing, and Brazilian Integralism is a separate movement.

territorial-expansion.rationale: Not part of integralist doctrine; the focus is ordering existing states to the spiritual end.

personal-loyalty-rule.rationale: Authority comes from God and serves the common good under law, not from feudal personal oaths.

bound-labor.rationale: Rerum Novarum insists on worker dignity and ownership; serfdom-like bondage is contrary to it.

no-neutral-knowledge.rationale: Integralists claim knowable truth, but also reject neutrality in the state; not an instance of the power-reflects-truth claim.

universal-morality.rationale: The natural law tradition holds moral truths knowable by reason; Immortale Dei grounds public law in them.

single-common-good.rationale: Immortale Dei says government exists for the common good and law should serve truth, not the shifting wishes of groups.

economic-freedom.rationale: Integralists tie lasting order to religion and virtue instead; liberty without limits is called licence.

rule-by-example.rationale: Rulers govern as fathers but Quanta Cura defends penalties for offenders, so moral example alone is insufficient; adherents split.

national-self-determination.rationale: The nation's will without reference to God is not sovereign, and integralists subordinate states to the Church.

force-without-un.rationale: The sources give no view on UN authorisation; integralists trace legitimacy to God and the common good, not to international bodies, but adherents have not settled the question.

reason-over-faith.rationale: The tradition holds faith and Church teaching as authoritative alongside reason, and condemns naturalism.

welfare-for-citizens.rationale: Catholic charity is universal while the state's duty is to its community; adherents differ and the sources do not decide it.

work-for-welfare.rationale: Rerum Novarum stresses workers' duty to work faithfully, so tying relief to work capacity is a plausible inference, not a stated rule.

class-collaboration.rationale: Rerum Novarum says rich and poor depend on each other and should cooperate like parts of a body.

sacrifice-heritage.rationale: Integralism seeks to preserve inherited institutions, the Church foremost.

racial-segregation-law.rationale: Catholic doctrine on the unity of mankind and the universal Church counts against racial classification in law.

state-class-instrument.rationale: The state exists for the community's welfare and class conflict is not natural, according to Rerum Novarum and Immortale Dei.

elite-replacement.rationale: A conspiracy claim not tied to the tradition.

national-mission.rationale: The mission belongs to the Church universal, not to a nation, in integralist theory.

patriarchy-structural.rationale: Integralists affirm husband's authority as natural but reject the framing of systematic disadvantage.

heritable-defect-limits.rationale: Rerum Novarum treats the family's rights as prior to the state, and Catholic doctrine on life rejects eugenic coercion.

night-watchman-state.rationale: The state is to promote the common good, protect religion and morals, and intervene for workers, which is far beyond a minimal state.

discourage-race-mixing.rationale: Marriage is holy and indissoluble, and the Church is universal; discouraging marriage on racial grounds contradicts this.

equal-moral-worth.rationale: Natural law holds a common human dignity, though integralism does not support equal rights regardless of religion in public law.

uniform-civil-code.rationale: Integralists favour a state that recognises the Church's role, with marriage under Church law; uniform code regardless of religion conflicts with this.

restrict-conversion.rationale: Immortale Dei says belief cannot be forced, but the state favours the true faith and may tolerate others; adherents differ on restricting conversion.

no-religion-state-schools.rationale: Immortale Dei and Quanta Cura condemn godless education and demand religious instruction in schooling.

consent-of-governed.rationale: Authority proceeds from God and not the people; consent is not the basis of legitimacy.

trade-surplus.rationale: Mercantile trade balance is not covered in the sources and no integralist principle settles it, so the answer is neutral.

population-transfer.rationale: Not an integralist teaching; Catholic doctrine on human dignity counts against it.

initiating-force-wrong.rationale: Quanta Cura defends state punishment of offences and Immortale Dei grounds coercive authority in God; absolute non-aggression is rejected.

competition-drives-progress.rationale: Rerum Novarum emphasises cooperation, not struggle, as the social principle.

freedom-as-non-domination.rationale: Republican freedom is not integralist; the tradition defines freedom as freedom from error and vice.

separated-powers.rationale: Not directly addressed; Church and state have distinct spheres, but a separated-powers state is not required.

vanguard-party.rationale: A Marxist-Leninist doctrine opposed by the Church; class rule is rejected.

priority-to-poor.rationale: Rerum Novarum says the state has a special duty to protect the needy workers who are the majority.

restrict-strikes-picketing.rationale: Rerum Novarum condemns workers' violence and promotes arbitration but also supports unions, so adherents are split on legal limits.

population-causes-poverty.rationale: Catholic social teaching attributes poverty to injustice and disorder, not population.

diversity-weakens-cohesion.rationale: Integralists seek unity of faith in public life but do not frame it as ethnic diversity.

offices-by-lottery.rationale: Authority comes from God and goes to those suited to rule; lottery contradicts it.

party-controls-media.rationale: Immortale Dei urges press supervision in the interest of religion and morals but a ruling party is not the mechanism.

party-commands-army.rationale: Integralist order has no ruling party; the army serves the state under legitimate authority.

pool-sovereignty.rationale: Integralists reject secular supranational unions, though a Catholic order is itself universal; the EU as such is not endorsed.

church-by-bishops.rationale: The Church is a perfect society with hierarchical authority, and Catholic government is episcopal and papal.

clerical-rule.rationale: Integralism holds that spiritual authority directs temporal authority indirectly, not that clergy hold the highest political office.

defeat-own-government-war.rationale: A Marxist revolutionary position; integralists accept the state's authority and the duty of obedience.

censor-art-for-virtue.rationale: Immortale Dei treats unrestricted publication as a source of evils and law is meant to promote virtue.

abolish-rental-housing.rationale: Rerum Novarum defends property rights and wide ownership but not bans on renting; a coercive ban is not taught.

rural-life-healthier.rationale: The sources do not rank rural against urban life; Rerum Novarum values land ownership by workers but makes no moral comparison of the two.

cultures-equal-different.rationale: The true religion is held superior and the state should not treat all faiths as equal.

sex-ed-in-schools.rationale: Education should follow religion and morality, and the family has prior rights over children's education, so the contemporary curriculum is opposed.

restrict-pornography.rationale: Law is meant to promote virtue and unlimited publication is called an evil, so restriction follows.

religious-exemptions.rationale: The state may tolerate other faiths to avoid greater harm, but Pink and others disagree on the extent; unresolved.

encourage-eccentricity.rationale: Integralists favour conformity of public life to virtue and truth, and reject liberal individuality.

constituent-assembly.rationale: Authority does not derive from popular sovereignty, so a constituent assembly is not the legitimate source of constitutions.

rich-countries-aid-poor.rationale: Catholic charity is universal, but Rerum Novarum addresses state duties domestically.

direct-election-head-of-state.rationale: Popular election is not the source of authority for integralists.

property-serves-common-good.rationale: Integralism ties property to the common good, and Rerum Novarum says state intervention is justified when it is threatened.

subordinate-church-to-state.rationale: Quanta Cura and Immortale Dei condemn state control of the Church and insist it is an independent perfect society with its own property and authority.

sacred-ruler.rationale: Immortale Dei holds that authority comes from God, but it does not make rulers divine or sacred by descent, and many forms of government are accepted.

character-from-environment.rationale: Catholic teaching holds that education forms people but also that nature, original sin and free will matter; adherents are split.

sovereign-above-law.rationale: Immortale Dei holds that rulers are bound by divine and natural law, which limits all human legislation.

leader-cult.rationale: Glorifying a ruler as the embodiment of the nation conflicts with the duty to worship God alone and with authority being held in trust from God.

class-struggle-under-socialism.rationale: Rerum Novarum rejects class conflict and socialism, urging cooperation between classes.

land-redistribution.rationale: Rerum Novarum defends private property, including land, against socialist redistribution.

apostasy-punishable.rationale: Quanta Cura backs state punishment of violators of religion; contemporary integralists differ on applying it to apostates.

material-conditions-drive-history.rationale: Integralism orders politics to a spiritual end, and Rerum Novarum rejects economic determinism.

no-bailouts.rationale: Rerum Novarum does not address bailouts; adherents are split between charity-first and common-good views.

moral-incentives.rationale: Rerum Novarum accepts wages and property incentives alongside duty; adherents are split.

capitalism-adapts.rationale: Rerum Novarum criticises both socialism and unchecked capitalism and makes no prediction of collapse.

labor-aristocracy.rationale: Rerum Novarum holds that classes should cooperate and that workers and owners need each other, against class-struggle theory.

entrenched-bill-of-rights.rationale: Quanta Cura condemns liberty of conscience and worship as rights, so a rights document shielded from the Church-guided common good is opposed.

elective-rulers.rationale: Immortale Dei holds that the form of government may vary so long as authority is ordered to God, so election versus heredity is indifferent.

resist-lawless-ruler.rationale: Immortale Dei requires obedience except when commands contradict God's law, and Leo XIII warns against sedition, so adherents are split.

noblesse-oblige.rationale: Rerum Novarum teaches that the rich must give from their surplus to the poor as a duty of charity and justice.

withdraw-from-politics.rationale: Integralism holds that politics must be ordered to humanity's spiritual end and that Catholics should take part in public life.

party-own-road.rationale: Quanta Cura condemns socialism and communism, so a socialist road is not endorsed.

antifascism-founding-value.rationale: Immortale Dei makes the Catholic faith, not any political creed, the public foundation of the state.

filial-duty.rationale: Catholic teaching on the fourth commandment and the family binds children to honour and support parents, and Rerum Novarum defends the family as prior to the state.

no-fault-divorce.rationale: Catholic teaching holds marriage indissoluble; integralists reject divorce, and the state must uphold the sacrament.

land-use-tenure.rationale: Rerum Novarum defends private property as a natural right, so common land ownership is rejected.

consumerism-harmful.rationale: Rerum Novarum condemns greed and the unlimited pursuit of wealth as a moral danger.

job-guarantee.rationale: Rerum Novarum defends a just wage and state protection of workers, but also warns against state overreach, so a state employer of last resort is not clearly accepted or rejected.

democratic-peace.rationale: Integralists reject liberal democracy as grounded in popular sovereignty and hold that the state should serve the Church's ends, so they do not accept spreading democracy as a means to peace.

no-duty-to-obey.rationale: Immortale Dei teaches that public authority comes from God and that obedience to lawful authority is a duty of conscience, which contradicts the claim that there is no general duty to obey.

industrial-unions.rationale: Rerum Novarum favors workers' associations, notably Catholic and mixed ones, but gives no preference between industrial and craft organization.

minority-conspiracy.rationale: Integralists have been accused of attributing plots to minorities, but the encyclicals address Masonic sects rather than ethnic or religious minorities; the claim is not part of the mainstream doctrine.

abolish-legal-marriage.rationale: Catholic teaching treats marriage as a public institution that the state should uphold, and Quanta Cura condemns the claim that marriage is merely civil.

local-production.rationale: Rerum Novarum favors widespread property and subsidiarity but does not take up local production or buying.

informal-organisation.rationale: Integralism stands for a hierarchical order under state and Church authority, and Rerum Novarum favors formal associations; small informal groups outside such structures are contrary to it.

religious-nation.rationale: Integralism holds that the state should profess the Catholic faith, but defines the political community by the common good and the faith of its people as its public religion, so the answer is split on whether religion defines the nation itself.

personal-possessions-private.rationale: Rerum Novarum defends private ownership of productive property as a natural right and rejects socialist common ownership, so the statement's common ownership of the means of production is rejected.

religion-illusion.rationale: Integralism holds that religion answers permanent spiritual needs and the state must be ordered to them, so religion will not fade.

women-equality-needs-economic-change.rationale: Rerum Novarum holds that the family and natural order, not economic transformation, shape the sexes' roles, rejecting the socialist programme.

socialized-care.rationale: Rerum Novarum defends the family as prior to the state and condemns state intrusion into it, so care stays with families.

neither-capitalism-nor-communism.rationale: Rerum Novarum rejects both socialism and unregulated liberal capitalism in favor of class cooperation, workers' associations and a Christian order.

punish-blasphemy.rationale: Quanta Cura condemns freedom of worship and conscience and defends the state's power to punish those who offend against the faith.

participatory-democracy.rationale: Rerum Novarum favours workers' associations, but integralism is hierarchical and rests on subsidiarity, not direct participation.

alienated-labor.rationale: Rerum Novarum criticises the condition of workers but defends private property; adherents split.

divine-source-of-authority.rationale: Immortale Dei teaches that civil power comes from God, not from popular sovereignty.

social-market-economy.rationale: Rerum Novarum combines private property and markets with state duties toward workers and the poor.

dynastic-succession.rationale: Immortale Dei accepts several forms of government including hereditary monarchy, so succession within a family is acceptable.

interest-free-mutual-credit.rationale: Rerum Novarum favours workers' associations, but its text does not address mutual credit banks.

property-franchise.rationale: Immortale Dei accepts varied forms of government and does not fix who votes, so adherents are split.

reification.rationale: Rerum Novarum criticizes the exploitation of workers but rejects the Marxist account of class relations behind this idea.

press-owned-by-wealth.rationale: Immortale Dei rejects unrestricted freedom of the press and of assembly, so the complaint about ownership is not its concern.

promulgated-standing-laws.rationale: Immortale Dei holds that rulers act under law ordered to the common good, though it allows prudential discretion.

racial-franchise.rationale: Rerum Novarum holds all men equal in dignity, and the Church is universal, so race cannot decide political membership.

boycott-minority-shops.rationale: Rerum Novarum teaches charity and justice toward all, so shunning a minority's shops is not endorsed.

reinterpret-religion.rationale: Quanta Cura condemns the idea that doctrine and the Church's teaching should adapt to modern progress, and Immortale Dei binds states to the Church's settled teaching.

state-promotes-atheism.rationale: Immortale Dei and Quanta Cura hold that the state must publicly profess and protect the true religion, so promoting atheism is the opposite of its duty.

abolish-police-prisons.rationale: Integralism holds that the state wields coercive power, including to protect the faith, so abolishing police and prisons contradicts its view of authority.

women-in-religious-leadership.rationale: Catholic integralism follows the Church's teaching that holy orders and the priesthood are reserved to men, so women cannot hold every office on the same terms.

shared-marital-authority.rationale: Catholic social teaching, which integralism follows, emphasises the family and the husband's headship in traditional readings, though with mutual duties, so equal shared authority is mostly rejected.

income-for-work-not-ownership.rationale: Rerum Novarum says labour deserves a just wage and warns against exploiting workers, but it also defends the property owner's income; it supports the principle moderately.

never-kill-self-defence.rationale: Catholic teaching, which integralism takes as binding, holds lethal self-defence and just war to be lawful, so the statement is rejected.

politics-spiritual-struggle.rationale: Integralism holds that political authority is ordered to humanity's spiritual end, and Immortale Dei frames politics as part of the Church's struggle against error.

independent-unions.rationale: Rerum Novarum calls workingmen's unions the most important of associations and says the state should not forbid them, though they are subject to religious guidance.

socialism-needs-workers-power.rationale: Rerum Novarum rejects socialism and class struggle, so working-class rule is not the test of a just order.

local-essentials-public.rationale: Subsidiarity and the common good could support public provision, but integralist sources do not take a position on local utilities.

second-chamber.rationale: Integralists accept several forms of government, so a second chamber is neither required nor opposed.

municipal-property.rationale: Rerum Novarum defends private property as a natural right and rejects collective ownership of the means of production.

family-wage.rationale: Rerum Novarum says wages must not fall short of supporting a frugal wage-earner and stresses the worker's family duties; the family wage was developed from it.

person-over-state.rationale: Rerum Novarum holds that man is older than the state and has rights the state must protect, though integralists subordinate the person to the common good and the Church.

spiritual-nature.rationale: Immortale Dei says political authority is ordered to humanity's spiritual end and that the state must profess and protect the true religion.

collective-bargaining.rationale: Rerum Novarum endorses workers' associations and negotiated wages, so group bargaining is favoured over isolated individual contracts, though class cooperation is stressed.

smash-state-machine.rationale: Immortale Dei grounds public authority in God and order, rejecting revolutionary overthrow; integralists want to capture and Christianise the state, not destroy it.

shared-human-nature.rationale: Immortale Dei and Quanta Cura rest dignity and rights on natural law and a created human nature, which is not to be redesigned.

religions-one-truth.rationale: Integralism holds that the Catholic faith is the one true religion that the state must profess; Immortale Dei rejects treating all religions as equal.

keep-nuclear-weapons.rationale: Nuclear weapons postdate the sources; adherents are split between just-war deterrence and papal calls for disarmament.

religious-equal-recognition.rationale: Immortale Dei and Quanta Cura hold that the state must profess and favor the true religion and reject equal standing for all cults.

democracy-is-procedure.rationale: Immortale Dei holds that power comes from God and that governments are judged by whether they serve the common good, not by elections alone.

defend-planned-state.rationale: Rerum Novarum rejects socialism and state abolition of private property, so a planned state is not worth defending for its economic system.

indirect-election.rationale: Immortale Dei accepts several forms of government and does not prescribe a method of selecting officers.

national-church-status.rationale: Immortale Dei says the state must publicly profess and protect the true faith and not treat all religions as equal.

simple-living.rationale: Rerum Novarum urges moderation and thrift but accepts property and trade; no stated view on self-sufficient living.

self-ownership.rationale: Integralism rejects unrestricted liberty and holds that persons and their actions are ordered to God and the common good, as Quanta Cura condemns liberty of conscience.

bypass-parties-groups.rationale: Rerum Novarum defends workers' associations and intermediate bodies, and integralism accepts several forms of government rather than leader-people bypassing.

no-denominational-politics.rationale: Integralism holds that the state must profess and protect the Catholic faith, rejecting religious neutrality, so politics is ordered by religion.

wife-divorce-without-consent.rationale: Catholic teaching holds marriage indissoluble and the state should uphold this, so a wife's unilateral divorce is rejected along with a husband's.

distribution-by-process.rationale: Rerum Novarum defends private property but demands just wages and a state duty toward the poor, so an unequal result is not just merely because the steps were voluntary.

unjust-law-not-binding.rationale: Catholic teaching holds that human commands against divine or natural law do not bind, which the integralists inherit from Leo XIII.

market-under-party-rule.rationale: Rerum Novarum rejects socialism and class conflict in favour of private property and class cooperation, so a communist-led economy is rejected.

missingStatements.text: The state should publicly profess and protect one true religion rather than treating all religions alike.
missingStatements.rationale: Immortale Dei says the state must profess and protect the true faith and not treat all religions as equal.

missingStatements.text: Temporal political authority should be subordinate to humanity's ultimate spiritual end.
missingStatements.rationale: This is described as a common theme of contemporary integralism and rests on Leo XIII and medieval papal claims.

missingStatements.text: Political authority comes from God rather than from the people.
missingStatements.rationale: Immortale Dei states that all public power must proceed from God and rejects sovereignty of the multitude without reference to God.

notes: The summary is for the Catholic integralist mainstream. Contemporary integralists differ on coercion in religion, compatibility with Dignitatis humanae (Pink says compatible) and on how far Vermeule's common good constitutionalism is integralist. Many answers are low-confidence inferences.
